bj40.name: Land Cruiser BJ40
bj40.notes: Diesel counterpart to the gas FJ40 on the same short-wheelbase 40-series body. Diff ratio is forum consensus, not factory-doc-confirmed; tire size unconfirmed.

bj41.name: Land Cruiser BJ41
bj41.notes: Rare JDM-only code between BJ40 (B engine) and BJ42 (3B engine) - confirmed real via VIN records and Toyota EPC, but absent from English Wikipedia. Curb weight is an estimate from sibling BJ40/42.

bj42.name: Land Cruiser BJ42
bj42.notes: Best-documented 40-series diesel code. Tire size (205R16) is an older flotation format, not parseable by the site's gearing calculator - a custom P-metric size in the form will still work.

bj43.name: Land Cruiser BJ43
bj43.notes: Curb weight source also lists the same figure for BJ44/BJ46 - possibly a genuine shared-body coincidence or a copy-paste artifact in the source; treat as approximate.

bj44.body_style: medium wheelbase hardtop wagon (BJ44V) or soft-top
bj44.name: Land Cruiser BJ44
bj44.notes: Uses the 2B engine, not B or 3B as often assumed - multiple sources agree on this. Diff ratio (4.875) is from a single source and notably differs from sibling codes' 4.11 - unconfirmed elsewhere, treat with caution.

bj45.body_style: long wheelbase pickup or troop carrier
bj45.name: Land Cruiser BJ45
bj45.notes: Production-year range is genuinely unresolved between sources. Curb weight is an estimate from sibling codes - figures found elsewhere were for 2F/2H-engined J45 variants, not this B-family diesel.
bj45.stock_transmission: H42 4-speed manual (H55F 5-speed was an aftermarket swap, not factory-stock)

bj46.body_style: medium wheelbase wagon (V-suffix), full-floating front/rear axles
bj46.name: Land Cruiser BJ46
bj46.notes: Successor to BJ44. Curb weight shares the same figure as BJ43/BJ44 on a single source - possible data reuse, treat as approximate.
bj46.stock_transmission: H55F 5-speed manual (one documented unit shows a 4-speed)

bj60.name: Land Cruiser BJ60
bj60.notes: Diesel counterpart to the gas FJ60/FJ62 on the same 60-series body - reusing that body's bay envelope. Never offered with a turbo despite some sources conflating it with 70-series 13B-T options. Years/hp have some source disagreement.
bj60.stock_transmission: H42 4-speed manual (H41F/H42F, A440F automatic, and H55F 5-speed also cited in some markets)

bj61.body_style: 4/5-door station wagon (high-roof and low-roof configurations reported)
bj61.name: Land Cruiser BJ61
bj61.notes: Same 3B block as BJ60 but a different (rotary/distributor-type) injection pump, reportedly milder output - no confirmed hp/torque figure found. Real but thinly documented; absent from Wikipedia entirely. Diff ratio is a single forum poster's explicitly-hedged estimate.

bj70.name: Land Cruiser BJ70
bj70.notes: Naturally-aspirated diesel counterpart to the turbo BJ71 on the same SWB 70-series body. hp/torque varied somewhat by year due to an injection-pump change after 1986.

bj71.name: Land Cruiser BJ71
bj71.notes: Turbo-diesel counterpart to BJ70. hp/torque figures conflict slightly between sources (120hp/217Nm vs 123hp/284Nm) - the lower figure is used here as the more widely corroborated one.

bj73.name: Land Cruiser BJ73
bj73.notes: Best-documented 70-series BJ code, good multi-source agreement on engine figures. Some export units used an alternate VM 5-cylinder turbodiesel - not modeled here.

bj74.name: Land Cruiser BJ74
bj74.notes: Turbo-diesel counterpart to BJ73. Engine figures agree cleanly across sources. Curb weight inferred from BJ73 by platform-sharing, not independently confirmed.

bj75.body_style: long-wheelbase pickup/cab-chassis (troop carrier hardtop also existed on this platform)
bj75.name: Land Cruiser BJ75
bj75.notes: Heavier than its SWB/MWB siblings, consistent with the longer pickup body. Later (1990-96) J75 variants moved to the 1PZ five-cylinder diesel (see PZJ75).

fj40.name: Land Cruiser FJ40
fj40.notes: The most iconic Land Cruiser code. Originally shipped with the earlier F engine (3.9L) before switching to 2F in 1975 - 2F used here as the single representative engine across both eras. Same body/frame as the diesel BJ40.

fj42.body_style: 4x2 (rear-wheel-drive) short wheelbase, Middle East market only
fj42.name: Land Cruiser FJ42
fj42.notes: IMPORTANT: this is a 2WD variant, breaking the 4x4 assumption most of this database makes - don't assume standard transfer-case/4x4 driveline logic applies. No independent spec sheet found beyond confirming it's a real, documented code.

fj43.name: Land Cruiser FJ43
fj43.notes: Documented as extremely rare, never officially imported to the US.

fj45.name: Land Cruiser FJ45
fj45.notes: The 4-door wagon body (FJ45V/LV) was discontinued in 1967 and replaced by the dedicated FJ55 wagon; pickup/hardtop continued to 1984.

fj55.body_style: 4-door station wagon, 2,700mm wheelbase - Toyota's first dedicated SUV-style wagon body
fj55.name: Land Cruiser FJ55
fj55.notes: Originally shipped with the F engine before switching to 2F in 1975 (2F used here as representative). Diff ratio changed to 3.70 late in the run (1978-80) per some sources - 4.11 used here as the longer-lived figure. Unique among FJ wagons for a tailgate-only rear (electric window, no separate hatch).

fj56.body_style: 4-door station wagon, 2,700mm wheelbase - same body as FJ55
fj56.name: Land Cruiser FJ56
fj56.notes: JDM-only chassis code Toyota assigned to the FJ55 body once it got the 2F engine in 1975 - export markets kept calling it FJ55. A naming distinction, not a mechanically different model - treat as identical to the post-1975 FJ55.

fj61.body_style: 4-door wagon, same body as FJ60/FJ62 (2,700mm wheelbase)
fj61.name: Land Cruiser FJ61
fj61.notes: Real code, but there's community debate about whether it was ever a distinct retail model vs. an internal/parts-catalog code bridging FJ60 to FJ62. No independently-sourced weight/diff/tire found - figures here are inherited from sibling FJ60/62.
fj61.stock_transmission: presumed H55F 5-speed manual, consistent with contemporary FJ60/62 (unconfirmed)
fj61.years: disputed: 1984-1988 per one source, Oct 1982-Nov 1984 per another (bridging FJ60 and FJ62)

fj62g.body_style: 4-door wagon (JDM 'VX' grade trim), same body as FJ62
fj62g.name: Land Cruiser FJ62G
fj62g.notes: JDM sub-code distinguished from FJ62V by its fuel-injected 3F-E, giving Toyota a passenger-class trim to sell in Japan. Weight/diff/tire inherited from the already-seeded FJ62 as a placeholder, not independently confirmed for this specific grade.
fj62g.stock_transmission: 4-speed automatic likely available (A440F/A440L family); manual availability unconfirmed for this grade

fj62v.body_style: 4-door wagon (hardtop, 'V' suffix), same body as FJ62
fj62v.name: Land Cruiser FJ62V
fj62v.notes: Effectively the base/export-equivalent FJ62 under a JDM-style V suffix, distinguished from FJ62G mainly by carbureted 3F vs fuel-injected 3F-E. Weight/diff/tire inherited from the already-seeded FJ62.

fj70.body_style: short wheelbase (2,310mm), pickup and 3-5 door wagon variants
fj70.name: Land Cruiser FJ70
fj70.notes: Gas-carbureted 70-series - relatively short-lived/niche compared to its diesel siblings (HZJ70/BJ70), which dominate surviving population and parts availability.

fj73.name: Land Cruiser FJ73
fj73.notes: One of the few 70-series gas variants explicitly documented as available with a 4-speed automatic.
fj73.stock_transmission: 5-speed manual (code unconfirmed); 4-speed automatic available on some units

fj75.body_style: long wheelbase (2,980-3,180mm), troop carrier and pickup body variants
fj75.name: Land Cruiser FJ75
fj75.notes: Gas 3F variant was relatively short-lived/niche versus its diesel siblings (HJ75/HZJ75/PZJ75), which dominate the long-wheelbase 70-series population.

fzj70.name: Land Cruiser FZJ70
fzj70.notes: 1FZ-FE output/tune varied across 1990-2009 production (212-240hp depending on market/era) - baseline seeded 1fz-fe figures used here for consistency across all FZJ codes.

fzj71.name: Land Cruiser FZJ71
fzj71.notes: A rare/regional variant with thin documentation - confirmed real but weight/diff/tire are estimates from sibling codes.

fzj73.name: Land Cruiser FZJ73
fzj73.notes: Multiple sources describe MWB gas 70-series units as extremely rare.

fzj74.name: Land Cruiser FZJ74
fzj74.notes: Confirmed real and rare/regional (frequently GCC-market). Weight/diff/tire not documented in sources found - flag for manual verification if precision matters.

fzj75.body_style: long wheelbase (~2980mm): cab-chassis pickup with tray, or troop carrier hardtop
fzj75.name: Land Cruiser FZJ75
fzj75.notes: Best-documented of the SWB/MWB/older-LWB gas codes. Weight is approximate, inferred partly from a diesel HZJ75 sibling with non-stock aux tanks.
fzj75.years: 1993-1999 (replaced the carbureted 3F-powered FJ75 in 1993; single code covers both pickup and troop-carrier bodies)

fzj76.name: Land Cruiser FZJ76
fzj76.notes: Introduction year has a genuine source conflict (1999 facelift vs. a 2007 Australia-specific reintroduction claim) - not resolved here.
fzj76.years: 1999-~2009 (market dependent; some sources tie a 4-door-wagon badge specifically to a 2007 addition)

fzj78.name: Land Cruiser FZJ78
fzj78.notes: The Australian end-of-sale date is a specific, sourced fact. Curb weight is the weakest field here - don't reuse figures from the later diesel-only generation, which is a different vehicle era entirely.
fzj78.years: 1999-2006 in Australia (confirmed - last petrol units withdrawn May 2006 as "FZJ78R-RJMRKQ"); continued to ~2009 in other petrol markets before the 1FZ-FE was replaced by the 1GR-FE V6

fzj79.name: Land Cruiser FZJ79
fzj79.notes: The later 4-door dual-cab pickup body (introduced 2012) is diesel-only (HZJ/VDJ79) and was never offered under this petrol code - don't conflate. Weight is approximate; don't reuse modern diesel dual-cab figures, a different vehicle generation.
fzj79.years: 1999-2006 in Australia (confirmed - last petrol units withdrawn May 2006 as "FZJ79R-TJMRKQ3"); continued to ~2009 in other petrol markets

hdj78.name: Land Cruiser HDJ78
hdj78.notes: Uses the non-intercooled 70-series tune of the 1HD-FTE (vs. the intercooled 100-series version of the same engine code, which is a different, out-of-scope chassis generation). 78=troop carrier, 79=pickup, per Toyota's 1999 model-number rename of the long-wheelbase 70-series.

hdj79.name: Land Cruiser HDJ79
hdj79.notes: Same drivetrain family as HDJ78 in a pickup/cab-chassis body rather than troop carrier.
hdj79.years: 1999-2007 (double-cab variant added 2012, still under the 79 designation but out of scope for this pre-80-series-era database)

hdj81.name: Land Cruiser HDJ81
hdj81.notes: Confirmed real via VINs and OEM parts catalogs (distinct from HDJ80 in Toyota's own model-code system), but NOT independently corroborated by Wikipedia's J80 article, which only names HDJ80R. Best-supported theory: a JDM/Europe-market code for the same generation, not a different wheelbase or later facelift. Spans both the 1HD-T (1990-95) and 1HD-FT (1995-97) engine eras - mapped here to the already-seeded 1HD-T for simplicity. Treat as effectively the same drivetrain family as HDJ80 unless JDM-specific trim distinctions matter to you.

hj45.name: Land Cruiser HJ45
hj45.notes: Diff ratio and weight are inferred from parts-compatibility/owner-reported figures across the era, not a single factory spec sheet.
hj45.stock_transmission: H41/H42 4-speed manual (exact code for this era unconfirmed)

hj47.name: Land Cruiser HJ47
hj47.notes: Successor to HJ45 with the larger 2H engine. Weight/diff figures are owner-reported/parts-catalog estimates, not a primary factory source.

hj60.name: Land Cruiser HJ60
hj60.notes: Diesel counterpart to the gas FJ60/FJ62 on the same 60-series body. Weight/diff/tire sourced from a detailed European-market spec sheet.
hj60.stock_transmission: H41F/H42F 4-speed manual (early), H55F 5-speed manual (1983-90); A440F automatic optional

hj61.name: Land Cruiser HJ61
hj61.notes: Turbo-diesel counterpart to HJ60. Well corroborated across sources - the best-documented of the H-family 60-series codes.

hj75.name: Land Cruiser HJ75
hj75.notes: Engine/years/diff ratio well corroborated across sources. Exact curb weight not found in a primary spec sheet - GVM of 3035kg was found instead, curb weight estimated from that.

hzj70.body_style: 2/3-door short-wheelbase hardtop wagon / cab-chassis pickup, leaf-sprung front axle
hzj70.name: Land Cruiser HZJ70
hzj70.notes: Years and SWB body well corroborated; curb weight/diff/tire could not be verified for this exact code.
hzj70.stock_transmission: H55F 5-speed manual (likely, unconfirmed for this specific code)

hzj71.body_style: 3-door short-wheelbase hardtop, coil-sprung front axle (post-1999 facelift successor to HZJ70)
hzj71.name: Land Cruiser HZJ71
hzj71.notes: Curb weight is from a specific 2004 JDM listing, not an official factory spec sheet.

hzj73.body_style: 3-door middle-wheelbase hardtop wagon, leaf-sprung front axle; never sold in the US
hzj73.name: Land Cruiser HZJ73
hzj73.notes: 1,950kg is for LX trim; ZX trim reported at 2,020kg, +40kg for the automatic.

hzj74.body_style: middle-wheelbase, successor to HZJ73 post-1999 facelift (coil-sprung front)
hzj74.name: Land Cruiser HZJ74
hzj74.notes: Curb weight is LX trim (+40kg for auto), from a search-aggregated spec rather than a primary factory sheet.
hzj74.stock_transmission: 5-speed manual standard; 4-speed automatic optional on some variants

hzj75.body_style: 2-door long-wheelbase pickup and troop carrier ("Troopy"), leaf-sprung front axle
hzj75.name: Land Cruiser HZJ75
hzj75.notes: Weight varies by year/body/source (1,981-2,071kg found). One forum source claims a larger 9.5in/4.3 diff vs. the 4.111 used here from a trip-prep spec sheet - genuinely conflicting, not resolved.
hzj75.stock_transmission: H55F 5-speed manual, single dry-plate clutch, dual-range 4WD

hzj76.body_style: 5-door semi-long-wheelbase station wagon, hardtop, up to 10-seater
hzj76.name: Land Cruiser HZJ76
hzj76.notes: Weight/diff/tire from a current-production factory export spec sheet; an older listing gives a lower ~2,190kg, likely an earlier/lighter trim.
hzj76.stock_transmission: H55F 5-speed manual; 4-speed automatic optional in some markets/years
hzj76.years: 1999-2004 (JDM run); reintroduced/continued for export markets from 2007

hzj77.body_style: 4/5-door semi-long-wheelbase station wagon/van (predecessor to HZJ76), leaf-sprung front axle
hzj77.name: Land Cruiser HZJ77
hzj77.notes: 2,000kg figure is for the HZJ77V-MNU variant; higher-trim HZJ77HV variants listed slightly heavier (2,080-2,090kg, +40kg for automatic).

hzj81.body_style: 5-door station wagon, full-time 4WD, same body as HZJ80
hzj81.name: Land Cruiser HZJ81
hzj81.notes: Confirmed real, distinct factory code (Toyota/JDM parts catalogs, dealer chassis-code listings) - but the exact engineering/market distinction from HZJ80 is unresolved even among long-time enthusiasts. Best-supported theory: JDM/Middle-East/Europe-market allocation of the same generation, not a different wheelbase or later facelift. Treat as effectively the same drivetrain family as HZJ80.
hzj81.stock_transmission: 5-speed manual (LSD-equipped per some listings); automatic optional in some markets

kzj70.name: Land Cruiser Prado KZJ70
kzj70.notes: General export/European-market 'light duty' variant (vs. JDM-only KZJ71) - uses a smaller 8.0in rear diff vs. 9.5in on heavy-duty 70-series per forum consensus.

kzj71.body_style: wagon (short wheelbase, 2/3-door; narrow-body 'G' and wide-body 'W' trims both seen)
kzj71.name: Land Cruiser Prado KZJ71
kzj71.notes: JDM 'Prado SX' trim - direct successor to LJ71 when the 1KZ-TE replaced the 2L-TE in May 1993.

kzj73.name: Land Cruiser Prado KZJ73
kzj73.notes: Confirmed Europe-only (LHD) model - direct successor to LJ73 with the 1KZ-T engine swap.

kzj77.body_style: wagon (long wheelbase, 4-door, up to 9 seats w/ rear jump seats)
kzj77.name: Land Cruiser Prado KZJ77
kzj77.notes: Engine inferred from the KZJ70/73/77 pattern (non-EFI 1KZ-T) rather than independently confirmed for this exact code. Its precise relationship to KZJ78 (narrow vs. wide body) isn't fully resolved across sources.

kzj78.body_style: wagon (long wheelbase, 4/5-door; G=narrow and W=wide body variants)
kzj78.name: Land Cruiser Prado KZJ78
kzj78.notes: Best-documented KZJ code. Replaced LJ78 in a May 1993 facelift. 1,930kg curb weight figure is specifically for the wide-body (KZJ78W).

lj70.name: Land Cruiser Prado LJ70
lj70.notes: Sources disagree on exact engine by year - some describe it continuing as a base/cheaper non-turbo (2L) trim alongside KZJ70 through 1996, others say the 2L/2L-T line was phased out by the 1993 1KZ update. 2L-TE used here as a representative engine; sold under various market names (Land Cruiser II, 'Bundera' in Australia).
lj70.stock_transmission: 5-speed manual (floor); coil-sprung front/rear, part-time 4WD, manual rear diff lock

lj71.name: Land Cruiser Prado LJ71
lj71.notes: Confirmed via Toyota's official 75-year vehicle lineage archive. Replaced by KZJ71 (1KZ-TE) from ~1993.

lj72.name: Land Cruiser Prado LJ72
lj72.notes: Verified real via OEM parts catalogs and multiple owner threads, distinct from other LJ codes by using the cheaper non-turbo 3L instead of 2L-T/2L-TE - a budget/export-market variant (Southeast Asia/Eastern Europe presence reported). Factory rim reported as 15x7in.
lj72.stock_transmission: 4-speed manual (differs from the 5-speed used on other LJ70/71/73 grades)

lj73.name: Land Cruiser Prado LJ73
lj73.notes: Confirmed via Toyota's official lineage source and a documented original-condition survivor. Replaced by KZJ73 in May 1993.

lj78.name: Land Cruiser Prado LJ78
lj78.notes: 4-cylinder-only chassis by design; the stock bay is noticeably tighter than the 6-cylinder 70-series variants (hzj78/hzj79).

lj79.body_style: wagon (long wheelbase, same body as LJ78)
lj79.name: Land Cruiser Prado LJ79
lj79.notes: Thinly sourced (essentially one detailed owner account plus registry references) but confirmed real - described by an owner as 'same as a 78 but with a 3L' rather than the 2L-TE used on LJ78. Treat production-year range as low confidence.
lj79.years: circa 1993-1996 (very limited production - one documented batch of 7 units imported to India in 1996)

pzj70.name: Land Cruiser PZJ70
pzj70.notes: Existence and engine confirmed by Wikipedia/auto-data.net. Curb weight from a secondary aggregator, not a primary Toyota document. Diff ratio/tire size unverified - don't assume same as RJ70's petrol-spec figures.

pzj73.name: Land Cruiser PZJ73
pzj73.notes: Existence confirmed via Wikipedia's PZ-engine article grouping PZJ70/73/75/77 as a set, corroborated by parts-catalog listings. No dedicated spec page found - engine specs interpolated from PZJ70/75.
pzj73.stock_transmission: 5-speed manual (not independently confirmed for this code)
pzj73.years: 1990-1996 (approximate, inferred from shared production window with PZJ70/75/77)

pzj75.name: Land Cruiser PZJ75
pzj75.notes: Confirmed via a dedicated spec page (2,980mm wheelbase, 4,885mm length, 3-door/6-seat) and forum references alongside HZJ75. Curb weight/diff/tire not published on that source - estimated here.

pzj77.name: Land Cruiser PZJ77
pzj77.notes: Existence well confirmed (Wikipedia, auto-data.net, Land Cruiser Heritage Museum survivor - an ex-Japanese fire-command vehicle, ih8mud). Described as largely Japan-only. Curb weight figures found online couldn't be traced to a primary source, so a conservative estimate is used instead.

rj70.name: Land Cruiser RJ70 ("Bundera" in Australia)
rj70.notes: Diff ratio documented by an Australian aftermarket-parts reference as 4.3 (Nov1984-Oct1985 build) and 4.55 (Oct1985-Aug1992 build) - 4.3 used here, not confirmed to apply outside that market. Curb weight is an enthusiast-forum estimate, not a factory figure.
rj70.stock_transmission: G52 5-speed manual (same unit as the Hilux) - not confirmed universal across all markets

rj73.name: Land Cruiser RJ73
rj73.notes: Full spec sheet found for dimensions/wheelbase (2,600mm)/fuel tank/brakes/steering, but curb weight and diff ratio were explicitly listed as unavailable on that source.
rj73.stock_transmission: 5-speed manual, almost certainly G52 given RJ70's confirmed fitment (not stated on the primary source)
rj73.years: 1984-1989 (some sources imply production closer to 1984-1993 - exact end date uncertain)

rj77.name: Land Cruiser RJ77
rj77.notes: Existence confirmed by an actual VIN'd museum unit (GCC/Middle East market) and an ih8mud for-sale listing. No factory weight/diff/tire data located for this specific code. Note: RJ75 was searched for and could NOT be verified as a real code - period parts catalogs consistently list the petrol RJ-series as just RJ70/RJ73/RJ77, so it was not added.
rj77.stock_transmission: 5-speed manual (one museum record lists '5F' - unclear if the same physical unit as RJ70's G52, or a distinct regional part code)
rj77.years: documented production from at least 1991; broader run likely tracks the same c.1985-1996 window as other RJ codes
